title: 'Very Good Ideas': Putin Says PM Modi Regularly Presses For Peaceful Resolution of Ukraine Conflict
text:
World
Swarajya Staff
Oct 02, 2026 | Updated 09:47 AM GMT+5:30

Russian President Vladimir Putin has praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his sustained efforts to end the Ukraine conflict, describing the Indian leader as having "very good ideas" aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions to bring the war to an end through peaceful means.
Speaking at a gathering, Putin revealed that Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite their "very good and even friendly relations", constantly raises questions about ending the conflict in Ukraine.
The Russian President noted that PM Modi has an "avid interest" in the matter and takes a neutral position while maintaining focus on ending the hostilities.
Putin expressed gratitude to the Prime Minister for promoting dialogue, diplomacy and mutually acceptable solutions to the war.
The Russian leader stated it was his duty to acknowledge PM Modi's contributions directly, adding that Moscow is thankful for the ideas put forward, though he did not elaborate on specific proposals.
PM Modi has repeatedly stated India's position that conflicts should be resolved peacefully, with New Delhi supporting the early return of peace and stability while prioritising humanitarian efforts.
The Prime Minister previously told Putin during Moscow talks in July that solutions are not found on battlefields but through dialogue and diplomacy.
India's diplomatic engagement has included visits to both Moscow and Kyiv, with Modi meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in August and assuring that India is ready to play an active role in peace efforts. PM Modi had stressed that both Ukraine and Russia must find ways to resolve the ongoing conflict, maintaining India's principled and humanitarian stance which has been appreciated by both presidents.
